impl_reports.summary:
C2b is done as one commit (970a6981, author Matt O'Grady <sewing.wader8c@icloud.com>). It is held locally on top of C2a (47d182fd) and the worktree is clean. The trailer grep over base..HEAD prints 0. There is one deviation from the plan: the workspace reqwest now asks for `system-proxy` (see deviations).

What the code does now:
- `crates/gglib-download/src/cli_exec/api.rs`: `create_hf_api` is deleted. There is a new `pub(super) fn hub_client(token) -> DefaultHfClient`, built as `HfClientConfig::default().with_optional_token(token)`.
  - `list_quantizations(model_id, token)` no longer takes the models dir. It gets the commit through `HfClientPort::get_commit_sha`, and the quant listing now sends `--token` too.
  - `fallback_file_search(model_id, token)` sends HEAD requests to `gglib_hf::build_file_url(model_id, pattern, None)`. hf-hub 0.4.3's `ApiRepo::url` built the same `{endpoint}/{repo}/resolve/main/{file}` URL.
- `crates/gglib-download/src/cli_exec/exec/mod.rs`:
  - `download` builds one `Arc<dyn HfClientPort>` from `request.token` and uses it for both `get_commit_sha` and `HfQuantizationResolver`, so the resolver now sends the token.
  - `check_update(repo_id, current_sha, token)` calls the private `check_update_with(&dyn HfClientPort, ..)`.
  - Both `spawn_blocking` wrappers and the ureq comment are gone.
  - The re-export in `cli_exec/mod.rs` drops `create_hf_api`.
- `crates/gglib-app-services/src/models.rs`: `check_upgrade` and `apply_upgrade` pass `std::env::var("HF_TOKEN").ok()`. `check_upgrade` no longer resolves the models dir. The file is 576→573 lines; its baseline is 576.
- `crates/gglib-cli/src/handlers/model/download/check_updates.rs` now uses `check_update` and `HF_TOKEN`. `&sha[..8]` is replaced by the existing `short_sha` from `update_model.rs`, made `pub(super)`, which already has two tests for short input. I used that instead of adding a second copy of the helper.
- `crates/gglib-cli/src/handlers/model/download/exec.rs` drops the unused `resolve_models_dir`.
- Manifests: the root `hf-hub` line, the cli and download entries, and the cli `use hf_hub as _;` are gone.
- Docs:
  - `loopback.rs` doc: the hf-hub clause is replaced by where the feature comes from now.
  - `loopback_tests.rs:99`: the literal is now `use hyper::Client;`.
  - The cli download README says check-updates sends `HF_TOKEN`.
  - The libssl-dev description reads "Required for llama.cpp's HTTPS support" in `scripts/check-deps.sh` and also in `crates/gglib-runtime/src/system/mod.rs`, the same sentence in the Rust checker. I checked llama.cpp e5a8d43's CMake: `LLAMA_OPENSSL` defaults to ON, and without OpenSSL it prints "HTTPS support disabled".
- New file `crates/gglib-download/src/cli_exec/exec/check_update_tests.rs`: a hand-written fake port (not mockall) and three tests:
  - `a_hub_that_names_the_recorded_sha_is_not_an_update`
  - `a_hub_past_the_recorded_sha_is_an_update`
  - `a_hub_that_names_no_sha_fails_the_check`

Lock:
- `cargo metadata --locked` refused the edited manifests (exit 101). Plain `cargo metadata --format-version 1` then regenerated the lock. It was not hand-edited and `cargo update` was not run.
- 952 → 936 `[[package]]` entries. Removed: exactly the 16 expected, and nothing was added.
- Every other change drops the version from a dependency reference now that only one version is left. These are in core-graphics, foreign-types 0.5.0, gglib-agent, gglib-app, gglib-app-services, gglib-axum, gglib-cli, gglib-download, gglib-hf, gglib-proxy, gglib-runtime, indicatif 0.18.6, iroh, iroh-relay, reqwest 0.13.4 and tauri. No checksum or source changed.
- `cargo tree --locked -i <pkg> --target all` now matches no package for openssl-sys, native-tls, ureq, reqwest@0.12.28, hf-hub, openssl or hyper-tls. Before, all of them were reached through hf-hub from gglib-cli and gglib-download.
- `git grep 'hf_hub|hf-hub' ':!Cargo.lock'` finds only the Python `hf_hub_download` (hf_xet_downloader.py and four comments in manager/mod.rs).

Text for the PR body (tier 1):
- Users authenticated only through `huggingface-cli login` lose gated-repo auth for check-updates, upgrade (the CLI, and the desktop app's upgrade check, which runs in the daemon) and `--list-quants`. When no token was passed, hf-hub's `ApiBuilder::new()` read `~/.cache/huggingface/token`, and gglib-hf reads no token file.
- check-updates and both upgrade paths now send the `HF_TOKEN` of the process that runs them. The daemon reads its own environment, so a daemon started without `HF_TOKEN` sends none. `--list-quants` sends `--token`.
- The commit lookup now uses gglib-hf's client, which has a 30 s timeout and retries up to 3 times. hf-hub's sync client had no timeout.
- The commit body carries the lock details and the proxy note.

Not covered by any test: the "drop the token from the client" mutation. No offline seam in gglib-download can see the Authorization header, because `HfClientConfig`'s token and base URL are `pub(crate)`. Catching it would need a public base-URL setter in gglib-hf, or an assertion on a Debug output that prints the token. The token → `auth_token` step is tested inside gglib-hf (`test_reqwest_backend_with_token`).

impl_reports.mutations:
Each mutation was a byte rewrite of the source file plus `touch`. Each file was restored from a saved copy, `cmp` confirmed it identical, then `touch`, and the tests were rerun green.
- M1, the hub error becomes "main" (in `check_update_with`, `.map_err(..)?` replaced by `.unwrap_or_else(|_| "main".to_string())`): `a_hub_that_names_no_sha_fails_the_check` went red (2 passed, 1 failed). Restored → 3 passed.
- M1b, gglib-hf answers "main" again (`.or_else(|| Some("main".to_string()))` before `.ok_or_else` in `crates/gglib-hf/src/client/repo_files.rs`): C2a's `a_model_info_that_names_no_commit_sha_is_an_invalid_response` went red (59 passed, 1 failed). Restored → 60 passed.
- M2, drop the token from the client (`hub_client` builds `HfClientConfig::default()`): SURVIVED. All 171 gglib-download tests stayed green. No offline test can see the header; see summary.
- M3, flip the comparison (`s != latest_sha` → `s == latest_sha`): `a_hub_that_names_the_recorded_sha_is_not_an_update` and `a_hub_past_the_recorded_sha_is_an_update` went red. Restored → 3 passed.
- M4, raw slice in the sha helper (done on an earlier local helper, before I switched to `update_model::short_sha`): the test for a short sha panicked red. The helper now in use is covered by the existing `short_sha_tolerates_shorter_input` in update_model.rs. A call-site mutation back to `&sha[..8]` in check_updates.rs would not be caught by any test, because `check_model_update` needs the network.
impl_reports.deviations:
1. The workspace reqwest gains the `system-proxy` feature (root Cargo.toml, with a 4-line comment). The plan did not ask for this.
   - Why: hf-hub's reqwest 0.12 default features were the only thing enabling hyper-util's `client-proxy-system` (checked with `cargo tree -e features`). Without it, `Matcher::from_system()` in hyper-util 0.1.20 reads env vars only, because the macOS SCDynamicStore and Windows registry reads are behind that feature.
   - Without my change, the plain lock regeneration also dropped hyper-util's `system-configuration` and `windows-registry` edges. Every shipped binary (gglib, gglib-app) would then stop following a proxy set in macOS or Windows settings. A desktop app launched from Finder has no shell env, so behind such a proxy it could lose Hub access.
   - With `system-proxy` on, runtime proxy behaviour is what it was, and the lock diff is exactly the 16 removals plus the version-drop rewrites.
   - To take the other option instead: delete `"system-proxy"` and the comment, rerun `cargo metadata`, and the hyper-util hunk comes back. The PR body would then need to name the loss of OS-proxy support.
2. The loopback.rs doc does more than drop the hf-hub clause. It now says the workspace's reqwest `system-proxy` turns the feature on, so the paragraph stays true, and the paragraph is rewrapped.
3. The libssl-dev sentence is also corrected in `crates/gglib-runtime/src/system/mod.rs`, the Rust twin of check-deps.sh that `gglib config check-deps` prints.
4. The CLI check-updates reuses `update_model::short_sha` (now `pub(super)`) instead of inlining `s.get(..8).unwrap_or(s)`. That helper was already there with two tests.
5. `exec.rs` (the download handler) no longer calls `resolve_models_dir(None)?`. It was used only for `--list-quants`. The queue path now no longer fails early on an unresolvable models dir; the daemon resolves its own.
6. `check_upgrade` in app-services no longer resolves the models dir either, for the same reason.
7. The cli download README gains one sentence: check-updates sends `HF_TOKEN`.
8. Out of scope and not done, a possible follow-up: `.github/workflows/docs.yml:58` and `release.yml:596` still install libssl-dev, and `check-deps.sh` still lists libssl-dev among the build tools.
9. The subject, and the PR-body text the orchestrator set, are used unchanged. One thing to check: the desktop upgrade check reads the daemon's own `HF_TOKEN`, so a daemon started without it sends no token.
impl_reports.review_focus:
1. Is adding `system-proxy` the right call, and is the claim behind it true? `cargo tree -e features -i hyper-util --target all` before the change: its only enabler was reqwest 0.12.28's `system-proxy`. After the change: enabled by reqwest 0.13.4's `system-proxy`. hyper-util 0.1.20 matcher.rs:238-247 gates the mac and windows system reads on the feature. reqwest 0.13.4 `Cargo.toml` has `system-proxy = ["hyper-util/client-proxy-system"]`, and proxy.rs:517 uses `Matcher::from_system()`. A macOS-only reviewer cannot see the Windows side.
2. The model-info endpoint changed. hf-hub's `info()` asked `/api/models/{repo}/revision/main`; gglib-hf asks `/api/models/{repo}`, whose `sha` is the default branch head. Error kinds and messages differ too (ModelNotFound, AuthRequired, and gglib-hf's retries up to 3 times with a 30 s timeout).
3. Token flow per path:
   - `--list-quants`: `--token` only. No HF_TOKEN fallback, as before.
   - check-updates: HF_TOKEN, where before it used only the token file.
   - The upgrade check: HF_TOKEN, where before it used `create_hf_api(None)`, so only the file token.
   - The upgrade download: HF_TOKEN goes to the commit lookup and now also to the resolver. Before, the commit lookup fell back to the file token and the resolver sent none.
4. Mutation M2 (drop the token) survives by construction. Decide whether that is acceptable, or whether gglib-hf should expose a base-URL seam.
5. The lock: diff Cargo.lock at 47d182fd against 970a6981 by package. Expect exactly 16 removals and 0 additions, with the other changes only dropping the version from a dependency reference. Check the hyper-util entry kept `system-configuration` and `windows-registry`.
6. Windows and Linux were not built on this Mac. `clippy-cross-os` in CI is the check. No cfg(windows) or cfg(linux) code was touched.
7. The rewrapped loopback.rs paragraph and the new root Cargo.toml comment are new prose. Check that each sentence is true at this commit.

defects.where: commit a4a94069 message, lock paragraph ("Every other change drops the version from a dependency reference to reqwest, console, indicatif, foreign-types, foreign-types-shared or wasm-streams")
defects.what: NON-BLOCKING (does not affect the PASS). The sentence leaves out two hunks. The lock diff also removes `"hf-hub",` from the dependency lists of gglib-cli 0.20.0 and gglib-download 0.20.0, and removing a reference is not dropping a version. A reader would probably take "losing hf-hub" to cover these, so the sentence misleads little, but it is not literally true.
defects.fix: Optional, if the message is amended anyway: "Every other change removes hf-hub from gglib-cli's and gglib-download's dependency lists, or drops the version from a dependency reference to reqwest, console, indicatif, foreign-types, foreign-types-shared or wasm-streams, of which one version is now left." Read it back at the new hash with --cleanup=whitespace.

defects.where: PR body (publisher), the Behaviour change and not-covered sections
defects.what: NON-BLOCKING. Three behaviour changes are real but not named. (a) The commit lookup used to go through hf-hub's ureq agent, which followed only the proxy environment variables (try_proxy_from_env). It now uses reqwest 0.13 with client-proxy-system, so on macOS and Windows it also follows the proxy set in the OS settings. (b) The lookup now has gglib-hf's 30 s timeout and 3 retries; hf-hub's sync client had no timeout and 0 retries. (c) A repo id without an owner/ part (e.g. "gpt2") now fails get_commit_sha with "Invalid model ID format"; hf-hub accepted it. Stored models cannot have such an id, because the download resolver already required owner/name. Also not covered by any offline test: M2 (hub_client drops the token) and M6 (the download resolver built from a tokenless client, which would falsify the message's "the resolver now sends the token too").
defects.fix: Add (a) and (b) to the PR body's Behaviour change paragraph as improvements. List M2 and M6 under not covered, with the reason: HfClientConfig's token and base_url are pub(crate) with no getter, and download() needs the network. Use the author's private-repo paragraph unchanged; I verified it.
